title: Freeze date gave no clear added spring break-up forecast gain at 59 lakes in 1981-2020
abstract: We tested whether an autumn freeze date improved the next spring break-up date forecast beyond a lake-specific time trend. We used NSIDC G01377 Version 1 and 59 lakes with at least 40 paired training seasons through spring 1980 and 20 paired test seasons in springs 1981-2020. Adding freeze date reduced equal-lake, variance-scaled test mean squared error by 8.62%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval was a change of -15.93% to +0.81%, so a gain was uncertain. Error in days fell from 11.45 to 11.01 days. With rolling 40-year training windows, the score fell by 1.99%, with an interval of -8.99% to +5.71%. In training data, 52 of 59 lakes had a negative freeze-date coefficient after trend removal. The median was -0.098 break-up days per later freeze day. This association did not establish a stable forecast gain or a physical cause. Selected frozen seasons, a sample dominated by Finland, no weather controls, missing records and uncertainty in the block length limit inference. The package gives original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and an independent scalar-regression audit. Source records stay outside the package.

display.caption: Change in variance-scaled test error when freeze date is added. Bars give conditional 95% five-year block intervals. Negative values favor freeze date. The right panel gives training slopes after trend removal. The primary interval includes zero.

citations.reason: NSIDC G01377 Version 1, 2023-10-11 CSV snapshot. We use paired dates from frozen lake seasons; full hash and path are in provenance.json.

Prior campaign result used the same ice snapshot and tested changes in temperature relations. We test next-spring break-up forecasts from freeze date with new code. Data overlap means this is not independent replication.
Prior analysis of trends and temperature controls. Our target is forecast gain from a preceding freeze date.
Prior review describes a possible weak within-season ice-on to ice-off connection. We test forecast value and do not claim a new mechanism.
Definitions of freeze and break-up dates; site conventions can differ.
